newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $77 mln trade surplus so far in May.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $77 mln trade surplus so far in May.

text.p: Brazil posted a trade surplus of $77 million in the first two weeks of May, with exports of $1.418 billion and imports of $1.341 billion, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said.
Asked to confirm the first positive trade result of the year, albeit only in the first six days of the month, a spokeswoman said, "That's right. A surplus."
The ministry said in its statement that average daily exports for the month so far stood at $236.3 million while average daily imports were $223.5 million.
In the first week, which consisted only of one day, exports were $278 million and imports $128 million.
Brazil posted a $951 million trade gap in April, bringing the deficit for the year so far to a whisker under $4.0 billion.
Government officials have said they expected a better result in May because of the continuing soybean harvest and measures to stem imports and boost exports.
